candidates.decision_relevance: Would show whether participation weakness or recovery persisted and how it aligned with price and leadership changes, rather than relying on proxy snapshots with changing membership.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily director outputs repeatedly cite point-in-time top-100 breadth proxies with changed membership hashes, while weekly reviews note missing quantitative breadth sequences.
candidates.metric_name: Constituent-level daily breadth observations with universe and membership identifiers
candidates.missing_history_problem: Existing endpoint counts are not comparable across captures when membership changes and cannot establish whether breadth deterioration preceded, persisted through, or recovered after price drawdowns.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would clarify the timing and persistence of reported flows relative to market rebounds and weakness, without treating stale settled rows or weekly totals as current confirmation.
candidates.evidence_reference: Multiple daily outputs identify October 16 as the latest supplied settled session and explicitly note missing intervening sessions; weekly reviews cite net ETF outflows but lack time-ordered observations.
candidates.metric_name: Settled daily BTC and ETH ETF net flows
candidates.missing_history_problem: Sparse settled-session observations and weekly aggregates do not reveal within-period flow sequence, persistence, or whether flows preceded or followed price changes.

candidates.decision_relevance: Would permit retrospective alignment of price moves with breadth, flows, and other observations, and distinguish a sustained decline from a rebound path hidden by weekly returns.

candidates.metric_name: Hourly BTC and ETH reference-price series
candidates.missing_history_problem: Window returns and weekly endpoints do not establish the magnitude, timing, or persistence of drawdowns and rebounds needed to assess sequence and hindsight concerns.
